notes:
This build had ZERO scripture voices — Hannah's vow, her answer to Eli, her naming
of Samuel and her giving him back were ALL paraphrased in the narrator's white voice.
Hannah is one of the great praying women in the Bible and the video never let her
speak. Fixed.

Lifted out as WOMAN (pink), verbatim KJV:
  w1a/w1b  1 Sam 1:11  her vow, split in two so the line is not one long breath
  w2       1 Sam 1:15  'No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit...'
  w3       1 Sam 1:20  'Because I have asked him of the LORD.'
  w4       1 Sam 1:28  'Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD...'
Eli's blessing is SCRIPTURE (light blue):
  s1       1 Sam 1:17  'Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition...'

1 Samuel is Old Testament — nothing here is `jesus`, and no one in this chapter is
Deity speaking, so there is no `god` beat either. Correct for the chapter.

LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: 1 Sam 1:16 ('Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of
Belial'). I am confident of the wording, but 'daughter of Belial' needs a paragraph
of explanation a first-time viewer does not have. Milk before meat — verse 15 alone
carries her whole answer. Nothing is paraphrased-as-scripture anywhere in this plan.

Narrator segments n2, n3b, n4, n5 and n6 were rewritten from paraphrase-of-Hannah
into retellings that follow her Old English, per the retelling rule. Every original
segment id is kept.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Year after year, Hannah went to the house of the LORD and came away with an empty lap.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The other wife mocked her for it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One year at Shiloh, Hannah slipped to the door of the tabernacle and prayed with a voice no one could hear — only her lips moved. This is what she said.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid,

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just look at me, she was saying. Remember me. Don't forget me. Give me a son — and I will give him back to You for the whole of his life. She asked for the one thing she wanted most, and promised it away in the same breath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Eli the priest watched her lips move with no sound coming out, and thought she was drunk.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No, my lord, she told him. I haven't been drinking. I'm a woman with a heavy heart, and I've been pouring my soul out to the Lord. She was not ashamed of the prayer. She just wanted him to know what he was looking at.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Go in peace, Eli said — and may the God of Israel give you the very thing you asked for. She went away, and her face was no longer sad. The LORD remembered her.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: Because I have asked him of the LORD.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A boy was born, and she named him Samuel — because I asked God for him. Every time anyone said that child's name, they were saying it again: I asked, and He heard.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She kept her word. I have lent him to the Lord, she said — for as long as he lives. When he was weaned, she brought him to the house of the LORD and left him there to serve.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Hannah prayed the prayer no one else could hear, and God answered. Your quiet prayers are heard too.

stills_wanted.ST1: This still now carries four straight beats — the whole vow. It should be Hannah alone at the doorpost of the tabernacle at Shiloh, close on her face, lips parted and moving with no sound coming out, eyes shut, hands empty in her lap. Not a wide temple shot: the moment is that nobody around her can hear a word of it.
stills_wanted.ST4: ST4 now has to work twice — Eli misjudging her, and then Eli blessing her. It should be the old priest seated by the door post, leaning toward her, his expression already turning from suspicion to gentleness, hand lifting slightly as he speaks. The moment his face changes.
stills_wanted.ST8: Hannah's hands letting go of the boy's shoulders at the door of the house of the LORD — the child stepping away from her toward the priest, her hands still open in the air where he was. The moment of giving him back, not a farewell hug.
